description:
FILED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07) by the #1241 probe matrix.  PRE-EXISTING â
reproduces on main `782bc37e` and on an unmodified `git archive` extraction.

    { my $r; print "ref=[", ref($r), "]\n"; }
    { my $r; print "ref=[", ref($r), "]\n"; }

        perl   ref=[]  ref=[]
        PCL    ref=[ARRAY]  ref=[ARRAY]        <- SILENT WRONG

ONE block (or a file-level `my`) is RIGHT, and that is the discriminator:
with a single occurrence the declaration lowers to `(p-let (($r :scalar
(p-undef))) â¦)` â a raw slot holding `*p-undef*` â and `p-ref` answers "".
With the name declared in two sibling blocks it lowers to `(p-let (($r :box
(make-p-box nil))) â¦)`, a BOX HOLDING NIL, and that is what `p-ref` gets
wrong.

THE CAUSE, in `p-ref` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp):

    ;; Old-format array reference (autovivified, single-boxed)
    ((or (listp inner) (and (vectorp inner) (not (stringp inner)))) "ARRAY")

`(listp nil)` is T, so a box whose value is the host null is reported as an
ARRAY reference.  A box holding `nil` is a legitimate spelling of undef â
docs/ir-spec.md Â§2.1 ("an array slot that was never assigned, or absent")
and Â§7's `p-return-value` rule ("a box holding `nil` yields `*p-undef*`,
never raw `nil`") â and every sibling reader agrees: `%pcl-definedp`
explicitly tests `(null v)` and answers undefined, which is why the same
probe prints `def=0` beside `ref=[ARRAY]`.  So `p-ref` is the one reading of
NIL that disagrees with the rest of the runtime (rule 11).

Whether the `(listp inner)` arm should recognise a proper LIST at all is the
second half of the question: no current producer stores a cons in a scalar
box (arrays are adjustable vectors), so the arm may be reducible to the
vector test alone.  MEASURE that before deleting it â the comment claims an
"old-format" producer.

FIX SHAPE: `(and inner (listp inner))`, or drop the `listp` disjunct if the
measurement says no producer needs it.  It changes `ref()` for every
undef-holding box, so the bar is the gate + the full sweep + the op/ and
lib/ companion legs, and a guard row asserting `ref(undef-box)` is "" beside
`defined` being false.

NOT FIXED IN s473b: out of that session's four-member scope (nested-element
autovivification), and `p-ref` is hot and reached by every `ref()` in the
corpus, so the change wants its own attribution run.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): ref() of a box holding host NIL answers "ARRAY" â `{ my $r; print ref($r) }` twice in a file gives ARRAY where perl gives ""
